questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Hydrogen atoms in the ground state absorb radiation of minimum frequency \(\nu_0\). In another experiment, the atoms are excited to an energy level from which a maximum of six distinct spectral lines are emitted during de-excitation. Assuming all possible transitions occur, the minimum frequency in the emission spectrum is:
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q1
questions.solution:
Min absorption is \(1	o2\): \(h
u_0=13.6(1-1/4)=10.2\)eV. 6 lines means \(n(n-1)/2=6\Rightarrow n=4\). Minimum emission energy is the smallest gap \(4	o3\): \(13.6(1/9-1/16)=13.6	imes7/144\)eV. Ratio to \(h
u_0=13.6	imes3/4\) gives \(\dfrac{7/144}{3/4}=\dfrac{7}{108}\). So answer is \(\dfrac{7}{108}
u_0\).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Energy levels A, B and C of a certain atom correspond to increasing values of energy, i.e. \(E_A<E_B<E_C\). If \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\) and \(\lambda_3\) are the wavelengths of radiations corresponding to transitions C to B, B to A and C to A respectively, which of the following relations is correct?
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q2
questions.solution: \(E_C-E_B=hc/\lambda_1\), \(E_B-E_A=hc/\lambda_2\). Adding: \(E_C-E_A=hc/\lambda_1+hc/\lambda_2=hc/\lambda_3\). So \(1/\lambda_1+1/\lambda_2=1/\lambda_3\Rightarrow \lambda_3=\dfrac{\lambda_1\lambda_2}{\lambda_1+\lambda_2}\).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The energy that should be added to an electron to reduce its de-Broglie wavelength from 1 nm to 0.5 nm is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q3
questions.solution: \(E=\dfrac{h^2}{2m\lambda^2}\propto\dfrac{1}{\lambda^2}\). Halving \(\lambda\) makes \(E\) four times: \(E_2=4E_1\). Energy to be added \(=E_2-E_1=3E_1\), i.e. thrice the initial energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An electron moves in a stationary Bohr orbit of a hydrogen-like ion of atomic number Z. Its kinetic energy is equal to the magnitude of the total energy of an electron in the first excited state of hydrogen. If R and \(\lambda\) are respectively the orbital radius and the de Broglie wavelength of the electron, then Z is:
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q4
questions.solution: KE \(=13.6Z^2/n^2=13.6/4\) (first excited state hydrogen magnitude) \(\Rightarrow Z/n=1/2\Rightarrow n=2Z\). Bohr quantization gives \(\lambda=2\pi R/n\Rightarrow n=2\pi R/\lambda\). So \(Z=n/2=\pi R/\lambda\).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The binding energy per nucleon of a nucleus X having mass number 20 is 8.0 MeV. The minimum energy required to remove one neutron from X, leaving the residual nucleus in its ground state, is 7.0 MeV. The binding energy per nucleon of the residual nucleus is approximately:
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q5
questions.solution: Total BE of X \(=20\times8.0=160\)MeV. Residual BE \(=160-7.0=153\)MeV over 19 nucleons \(=153/19\approx8.05\)MeV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A photosensitive metal surface has a threshold wavelength \(\lambda_0\). It is illuminated successively by monochromatic radiations of wavelengths \(\lambda_0/2\) and \(\lambda_0/3\). If \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) are the de Broglie wavelengths of the fastest photoelectrons emitted in the two cases, respectively, then \(\lambda_1/\lambda_2\) is:
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q6
questions.solution: \(KE_1=hc/(\lambda_0/2)-hc/\lambda_0=hc/\lambda_0\). \(KE_2=3hc/\lambda_0-hc/\lambda_0=2hc/\lambda_0\). De Broglie \(\lambda\propto1/\sqrt{KE}\), so \(\lambda_1/\lambda_2=\sqrt{KE_2/KE_1}=\sqrt2\).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The binding energies per nucleon of deuterium, tritium and helium nuclei are 1.1 MeV, 2.8 MeV and 7.1 MeV, respectively. Consider the fusion reaction \({}_1^2H+{}_1^3H\to{}_2^4He+{}_0^1n\). The reactant nuclei are initially at rest. Assuming that the products move non-relativistically and their masses are proportional to their mass numbers, the kinetic energy of the helium nucleus is approximately:
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q15
questions.solution: Total Q value \(=4\times7.1-(2\times1.1+3\times2.8)=28.4-10.6=17.8\)MeV. By momentum conservation KE splits inversely as mass: \(KE_{He}=\dfrac{m_n}{m_n+m_{He}}\times17.8=\dfrac{1}{5}\times17.8=3.56\)MeV.

questions.solution: Energy released \(=2(119\times8.5)-238\times7.6=2023-1808.8=214.2\approx214\)MeV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: When a metallic surface is illuminated with monochromatic light of wavelength \(\lambda\), the stopping potential is \(V_0\). When the wavelength is changed to \(\lambda/2\), the stopping potential becomes \(3V_0\). If the same surface is subsequently illuminated with photons having momentum \(\dfrac{3h}{2\lambda}\), the stopping potential is:
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q19
questions.solution: \(eV_0=hc/\lambda-\phi\); \(3eV_0=2hc/\lambda-\phi\). Subtracting: \(hc/\lambda=2eV_0\Rightarrow\phi=eV_0\). Photon energy \(=pc=\dfrac{3hc}{2\lambda}=3eV_0\). New \(eV_{stop}=3eV_0-eV_0=2eV_0\Rightarrow V_{stop}=2V_0\).

questions.text: Wavelengths belonging to Balmer series lying in the range of 450 nm to 750 nm were used to eject photoelectrons from a metal surface whose work function is 2.0 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectron is k eV, find value of 100k and roundoff to nearest integer. (Take hc = 1242 eV nm.)
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q21
questions.solution: Balmer lines in range: \(n=4\to2\): \(E=13.6(1/4-1/16)=2.55\)eV (\(\lambda\approx487\)nm, in range); \(n=3\to2\): 1.89eV (657.6nm). \(n=5\to2\) gives \(\lambda\approx435\)nm — out of range. Highest energy in range \(=2.55\)eV. \(KE_{max}=2.55-2.0=0.55\)eV \(=k\). \(100k=55\).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A hydrogen-like atom of atomic number Z is in an excited state of quantum number 2n. It can emit a maximum energy photon of 204 eV. If it makes a transition to the quantum state N, a photon of energy 40.8 eV is emitted. Calculate the atomic number Z. Ground state energy of hydrogen atom is 13.6 eV
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q22
questions.solution: Max energy photon (2n→1): \(13.6Z^2(1-1/(2n)^2)=204\). Transition (2n→n): \(13.6Z^2\cdot\dfrac{3}{4n^2}=40.8\). Dividing gives \(\dfrac{1-1/(4n^2)}{3/(4n^2)}=5\Rightarrow 4n^2-1=15\Rightarrow n=2\). Substituting back: \(13.6Z^2\times3/16=40.8\Rightarrow Z^2=16\Rightarrow Z=4\).

questions.solution: \(R\propto A^{1/3}\). \((A/4)^{1/3}=14^{1/3}\Rightarrow A/4=14\Rightarrow A=56\).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The number of photons falling per second on a completely darkened plate to produce a force of \(6.62\times10^{-5}\)N is \(n\times10^{22}\). If the wavelength of the light falling is \(5\times10^{-7}\)m, then what is the value of n? (Take \(h=6.62\times10^{-34}\)Js)
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q24
questions.solution: Photon momentum \(=h/\lambda\). Force \(=N\times h/\lambda\Rightarrow N=F\lambda/h=\dfrac{6.62\times10^{-5}\times5\times10^{-7}}{6.62\times10^{-34}}=5\times10^{22}\). So \(n=5\).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion: As a salt such as NaCl dissolves, the \(Na^+\) and \(Cl^-\) ions leaving the crystal lattice acquire far greater freedom.
Reason: In thermodynamic terms, the formation of solution occurs with a favourable change in free energy, i.e., \(\Delta H\) has a high positive value and \(T\Delta S\) a low negative value.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q33
questions.solution: Assertion is correct — ions gain translational freedom on dissolving (entropy increases). Reason is wrong: dissolution is favoured because \(T\Delta S\) is high and positive (entropy increase), not a "low negative value". So assertion true, reason false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Three samples of 100 g of water (samples I, II and III), initially kept at 1 atm pressure and 298 K were given the following treatments.
Sample I was heated to 320 K and cooled to 298 K
Sample II was heated to 300 K, cooled to 273 K and heated to 298 K

options: I and III are the same, II is lower than that of I and III
I, II and III are the same
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q35

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The standard entropy of \(X_2,Y_2\) and \(XY_3\) are 60, 40 and 50 \(J\,K^{-1}mol^{-1}\), respectively. For the reaction \(\tfrac12X_2+\tfrac32Y_2\to XY_3\), \(\Delta H=-30\,kJ\); to be at equilibrium the temperature will be
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q36
questions.solution: \(\Delta S=50-[\tfrac12(60)+\tfrac32(40)]=50-90=-40\,J/K\). At equilibrium \(\Delta G=0\Rightarrow T=\Delta H/\Delta S=\dfrac{-30000}{-40}=750\)K.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Match the following.
List-I (Type of reaction)
A. Combination reaction
B. Decomposition reaction
C. Disproportionation reaction
D. Displacement reaction

List-II (Unbalanced equation)
(i) \(AgNO_3+CaCl_2\to AgCl+Ca(NO_3)_2\)
(ii) \(Cl_2\to Cl^-+ClO_3^-\)
(iii) \(Mg+N_2\to Mg_3N_2\)
(iv) \(KClO_3\to KCl+O_2\)
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q37
questions.solution: Combination: Mg+N₂→Mg₃N₂ (iii). Decomposition: KClO₃→KCl+O₂ (iv). Disproportionation: Cl₂→Cl⁻+ClO₃⁻ (ii). Displacement: AgNO₃+CaCl₂→AgCl+Ca(NO₃)₂ (i). So A-(iii); B-(iv); C-(ii); D-(i).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Spontaneous process
B. Isothermal and isobaric process
C. \(\Delta H\) reaction
D. Exothermic process

List-II
(I) \(\Delta H<0\)
(II) \(\Delta T=0,\Delta P=0\)
(III) \(\Delta G_{T,P}<0\)
(IV) \(\Sigma BE_{Reactants}-\Sigma BE_{Products}\)
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q38
questions.solution: Spontaneous: \(\Delta G_{T,P}<0\) (III). Isothermal & isobaric: \(\Delta T=0,\Delta P=0\) (II). \(\Delta H\) reaction \(=\Sigma BE_{reactants}-\Sigma BE_{products}\) (IV). Exothermic: \(\Delta H<0\) (I). So (A)-(III),(B)-(II),(C)-(IV),(D)-(I).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Consider the following statements.
I. The entropy in isolated system with only p-V work is always maximised at equilibrium.
II. It is possible for the entropy of a closed system to increase substantially in an irreversible process.
III. Without the help of an external agency, a spontaneous process cannot be reversed.
IV. \(\Delta S_{system}\) is zero for a reversible process in an isolated system.

questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT-05 HTML answer key · Q41
questions.solution: All four statements are correct standard thermodynamic principles: entropy maximisation at equilibrium in an isolated system, entropy increase in irreversible processes, irreversibility of spontaneous processes, and zero \(\Delta S\) for a reversible process in an isolated system.
